title: Anti-Inflammatory Diet: What It Is and What the Evidence Shows
meta_description: An anti-inflammatory diet emphasizes whole, plant-rich, polyphenol-heavy foods. Trials show Mediterranean-style eating lowers markers of inflammation. Here’s the evidence and the food list.
product_bridge_blurb: Tea and warming spices fit an anti-inflammatory pattern.
body_html:
An “anti-inflammatory diet” isn’t a strict program — it’s a pattern: mostly whole, minimally processed, plant-rich foods, with plenty of polyphenols and healthy fats. The best-studied version is the Mediterranean dietary pattern.

What the evidence shows

A meta-analysis of intervention trials found that Mediterranean-style eating improved markers of inflammation and endothelial (blood-vessel) function. A more recent systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials likewise concluded the Mediterranean diet reduces inflammation in adults. The effect is real, though “inflammation markers” are a step removed from any single health outcome.

The food pattern

  • Build on: vegetables, fruit, legumes, whole grains, nuts, olive oil, fish, herbs and spices, tea.
  • Limit: ultra-processed foods, refined sugar, and excess red/processed meat.

Where tea and spices fit

Tea, ginger, turmeric, and cinnamon are all polyphenol- or compound-rich foods that fit an anti-inflammatory pattern. They’re a small piece of the picture — the overall diet matters far more than any one ingredient.

Key Components of an Anti-Inflammatory Diet

An anti-inflammatory diet includes a range of whole, plant-rich foods and certain types of fish, which have been shown to reduce markers of inflammation.

  • Camellia sinensis var. assamica, a cultivar used in tea production, contains anti-inflammatory catechins.
  • Steeping leaf releases anti-inflammatory theaflavins, which may contribute to the anti-inflammatory effects of tea consumption.
  • Fatty fish like salmon reduce inflammation with omega-3 fatty acids, which have been shown to have anti-inflammatory properties.
  • Olive oil is rich in oleocanthal, an anti-inflammatory compound that may help reduce inflammation.
  • Berries like blueberries are high in anti-inflammatory anthocyanins, which have been linked to reduced inflammation.
  • Cruciferous vegetables like broccoli contain anti-inflammatory sulforaphane, which may help reduce inflammation.

Food Choices and Inflammation

Research suggests that incorporating these foods into an anti-inflammatory diet may help reduce markers of inflammation, although effects are typically modest and more research is needed to fully understand the relationships between these foods and inflammation.

Summary of Anti-Inflammatory Foods

In summary, an anti-inflammatory diet emphasizes whole, plant-rich foods, including leaf from Camellia sinensis var. assamica, fatty fish like salmon, olive oil, berries like blueberries, and cruciferous vegetables like broccoli, which have been shown to contain anti-inflammatory compounds.

faqs.a: A pattern of mostly whole, plant-rich, polyphenol-heavy foods with healthy fats — best exemplified by the Mediterranean diet. It is a way of eating, not a strict program.

faqs.q: Does an anti-inflammatory diet actually work?
faqs.a: Meta-analyses of trials show Mediterranean-style eating lowers markers of inflammation. Inflammation markers are one step removed from specific outcomes, but the pattern is well supported and broadly healthy.
